extracted.intended_audience: research mathematicians working on Mochizuki's inter-universal Teichmüller theory, Frobenioids, and arithmetic geometry
extracted.subtask_description: Constructions and structural properties (existence/uniqueness/isomorphisms, symmetries, semi-simplifications, evaluation maps) of theta/gaussian/constant/semisimplified monoids and their Frobenioid-theoretic analogues in IUT theory at bad, good nonarchimedean, and archimedean primes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Isomorphism-of-categories convention
rubrics_metrics.description: An 'isomorphism of categories' is to be understood as an isomorphism class of equivalences of categories; in the Frobenioid context, various Frobenioids indexed by a subscript '|t| ∈ |Fl|' are to be considered determined up to an isomorphism of the identity functor (i.e., corresponding to an 'inner automorphism' independent of |t|).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When there is danger of confusion, resort to the original 'monoid-theoretic formulations' of Corollaries 3.5, 3.6 (i.e., treat via monoid-level statements rather than category-level identifications).

rubrics_metrics.name: Restriction to decomposition groups indexed by profinite conjugacy classes of cusps
rubrics_metrics.description: Construction algorithms for Gaussian monoids and related splittings involve restriction to decomposition groups of torsion points indexed (via a functorial algorithm) by profinite conjugacy classes of cusps, which are subject to a certain F3±-symmetry.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Interpret this symmetry as restriction to the portion labeled by the valuation v under consideration of the F3±-symmetry associated to a D-Θ±ell-Hodge theater; these constructions revolve around labeled copies of local Frobenioids at v determined by submonoids of the appropriate local objects.

rubrics_metrics.name: Formation of holomorphic or mono-analytic processions
rubrics_metrics.description: After executing construction algorithms for split Gaussian monoids and observing the relevant F-symmetry, one may form holomorphic or mono-analytic processions indexed by subsets of |Fl| (or F_l), compatible with earlier ' |Fl|-processions'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See references to [IUTchI], Proposition 6.9 and Proposition 4.11: these processions arise naturally once the split Gaussian monoid constructions and symmetries are in place.

rubrics_metrics.name: Local passage and label identification (Prop. 6.7 assignment)
rubrics_metrics.description: Applying the algorithm of [IUTchI], Proposition 6.7, passes to the local portion at v of a D-ΘNF-Hodge theater by removing the label 0 and identifying it with the complement (i.e., with F_l); at the level of local Frobenioids this corresponds to certain isomorphisms of monoids described in the first displays of Corollaries 3.5(iii), 3.6(iii).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: At label level this is the assignment removing 0 and reinterpreting labels as elements of F_l; use the corresponding monoid isomorphisms to realize the local theory and relate it to F_l-symmetries.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of F_l-symmetry to relate bad and good valuations and global theory
rubrics_metrics.description: The F_l-symmetries obtained after localization are well-suited to relating the §3 theory at v ∈ Vbad to valuations in Vgood and to the global theory of [IUTchI], §5; the global theory allows relating multiplicative and additive structures of a global number field.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the F_l-indexed processions and compatibility statements (cf. [IUTchI], Proposition 4.11 and Proposition 6.9) to form global compatibilities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consequences of conjugate synchronization — monoid isomorphisms (a)
rubrics_metrics.description: There exist isomorphisms of monoids Ψcns(MΘ*)|t1| ∼→ Ψcns(MΘ*)|t2|; (Ψ†Cv)|t1| ∼→ (Ψ†Cv)|t2|; and (Ψ†Cv)|t| ∼→ Ψcns(MΘ*)|t|, where the third isomorphism is well-defined up to an inner automorphism indeterminacy independent of |t|.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These isomorphisms are direct technical consequences of the conjugate synchronization and are referenced to Corollaries 3.5(i) and 3.6(i).

rubrics_metrics.name: Consequences of conjugate synchronization — diagonal submonoids (b)
rubrics_metrics.description: Construction of well-defined diagonal submonoids (diagonal embeddings / 'constant distributions') Ψcns(MΘ*)(|Fl|) ⊆ ∏_{|t|∈|Fl|} Ψcns(MΘ*)|t| and Ψcns(MΘ*)(F_l) ⊆ ∏_{|t|∈F_l} Ψcns(MΘ*)|t|.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These diagonal embeddings arise as formal consequences of the isomorphisms in (a) and correspond to 'constant distributions' in the categorical embeddings described earlier (Definition 3.8(iii)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Consequences of conjugate synchronization — 0-label isomorphisms (c)
rubrics_metrics.description: Well-defined isomorphisms Ψcns(MΘ*)0 ∼→ Ψcns(MΘ*)(F_l) and (Ψ†Cv)0 ∼→ (Ψ†Cv)(F_l) (Corollaries 3.5(iii), 3.6(iii)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These follow from the conjugate synchronization and the label-identification process; they are formal consequences of (a).

rubrics_metrics.name: Consequences of conjugate synchronization — restriction to units (d)
rubrics_metrics.description: Restriction to the units of the composite isomorphism of monoids Ψ†FΘ_{v,α} ∼→ ΨFξ(†F_v) that appears in the third display of Corollary 3.6(ii); this restriction is central for composing the Θ-link with certain composite arrows (the 'isomorphism of monoids' appearing in (d)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This restriction to units provides the main application of conjugate synchronization in §4 (the 'coricity of O×' context) and is an alternate formulation of the portion of (a) concerning units when |t| ∈ F_l.

rubrics_metrics.name: Post-anabelian monoid/Frobenioid context requirement for isomorphisms
rubrics_metrics.description: The isomorphisms of monoids that appear in the Θ-link or in Corollary 3.6(ii) make sense only when one works with post-anabelian abstract monoids/Frobenioids (i.e., 'Frobenius-like' structures).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is a constraint on the ambient objects: one must treat monoids/Frobenioids in the post-anabelian abstract setting for the stated isomorphisms to be meaningful.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prop. 4.1(i) — Existence of constant (functorial) monoids Ψcns(Gv), Ψcns(Πv)
rubrics_metrics.description: A functorial group-theoretic algorithm in the topological group Gv constructs an ind-topological submonoid Ψcns(Gv) ⊆ lim_{J} H^1(J, μ_Z(Gv)) equipped with its natural Gv-action; similarly one obtains Ψcns(Πv) in Πv.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: J ranges over open subgroups; this is the 'constant monoids' construction (cf. [AbsTopIII], Corollary 1.10(b) and Proposition 3.1(ii) in the Vbad case).

rubrics_metrics.name: Prop. 4.1(ii) — Mono-analytic semi-simplifications and distinguished element
rubrics_metrics.description: A functorial algorithm constructs a topological monoid R_{≥0}(Gv) and a distinguished element log_{Gv}(pv) ∈ R_{≥0}(Gv); define Ψss_cns(Gv) := Ψcns(Gv)× × R_{≥0}(Gv) as a 'semi-simplified version' of Ψcns(Gv).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The construction uses the realification (rlf) of Ψcns(Gv)/Ψcns(Gv)× and yields canonical elements used later in evaluation maps (cf. [IUTchI], Example 3.5(iii)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Prop. 4.1(iii) — Labels, F3±_l-symmetries, and symmetrizing isomorphisms
rubrics_metrics.description: For t ∈ LabCusp±(Πv) the Δ±_v-outer action (F3±_l) induces symmetrizing isomorphisms between labeled pairs (Gv(Πv)_t, Ψcns(Πv)_t) for distinct t; these determine diagonal submonoids Ψcns(Πv)(|Fl|) ⊆ ∏_{|t|} Ψcns(Πv)|t| and an isomorphism Ψcns(Πv)0 ∼→ Ψcns(Πv)(F_l).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These symmetrizing isomorphisms are the local analogues of conjugate synchronization (cf. Corollary 3.5(i) and Corollary 2.4(iii)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Prop. 4.1(iv) — Theta and Gaussian monoid constructions and evaluation isomorphism
rubrics_metrics.description: Define Ψenv(Πv) := Ψcns(Πv)× × R_{≥0}·log_{Πv}(pv)·log_{Πv}(Θ) (formal symbol) and Ψgau(Πv) as the product indexed by j∈F_l of copies of Ψcns(Πv)× × R_{≥0}(Πv)^j; there is a functorial group-theoretic algorithm constructing Ψenv(Πv), Ψgau(Πv) with natural Gv(Πv)-actions/splittings and a formal evaluation isomorphism Ψenv(Πv) ∼→ Ψgau(Πv) sending the formal log to the tuple (. . . , j^2·log_{Πv}(pv), . . .).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The evaluation restricts to the identity on Ψcns(Πv)× and is compatible with Gv-actions and splittings (cf. Corollary 3.5(ii)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Multiradiality/uniradiality formal analogues
rubrics_metrics.description: At v ∈ Vgood (Vnon), the construction of Ψcns(Πv) is uniradial, while the constructions of Ψss_cns(Πv), Ψenv(Πv), Ψgau(Πv), and the isomorphism Ψenv(Πv) ∼→ Ψgau(Πv) are multiradial.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is a tautological formal generalization of the multiradiality/uniradiality statements at v ∈ Vbad (cf. Proposition 3.4 and Corollary 3.7); the global analogue will specialize appropriately.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prop. 4.2(i) — Frobenioid-theoretic constant monoid isomorphism
rubrics_metrics.description: There exists a unique Gv(†Πv)-equivariant isomorphism of monoids Ψ†F_v ∼→ Ψcns(†Πv) (cf. Proposition 3.3(ii) in Vbad case).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This identifies the Frobenioid-theoretic monoid arising from †F_v with the constant monoid constructed from †Πv, up to the usual inner automorphism indeterminacies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prop. 4.2(ii) — Frobenioid mono-analytic semi-simplifications and distinguished element
rubrics_metrics.description: There exists a unique †Gv-equivariant μ_Z×-orbit of isomorphisms Ψ×†F_v ∼→ Ψcns(†Gv)× and a unique isomorphism ΨR†F_v := (Ψ†F_v / Ψ×†F_v)^{rlf} ∼→ ΨR_cns(†Gv) sending the distinguished element to log_{†Gv}(pv); define Ψss†F_v and obtain a natural isomorphism Ψss†F_v ∼→ Ψss_cns(†Gv).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These uniqueness and compatibility statements are required for transferring the semi-simplified structures between Frobenioid and constant constructions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prop. 4.2(iii) — Frobenioid labels, symmetries, and conjugate synchronization
rubrics_metrics.description: The isomorphism of (i) determines, for each t ∈ LabCusp±(†Πv), compatible isomorphisms (Ψ†F)_t ∼→ Ψcns(†Πv)_t well-defined up to an inner automorphism independent of t, as well as F3±-symmetrizing isomorphisms induced by the †Δ±_v/†Δcor_v action; these produce diagonal submonoids and an isomorphism (Ψ†F)0 ∼→ (Ψ†F)(F_l).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is the Frobenioid-level counterpart of the Πv-level symmetries and diagonal embeddings (cf. Corollary 3.6(i),(iii)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Prop. 4.2(iv) — Frobenioid theta and gaussian monoids and natural isomorphisms
rubrics_metrics.description: Define Ψ†FΘ_v and ΨFgau(†F_v) via the isomorphisms of (i)-(iii) induced by Ψenv(†Πv) and Ψgau(†Πv); there is a collection of natural isomorphisms Ψ†FΘ_v ∼→ Ψenv(†Πv) ∼→ Ψgau(†Πv) ∼→ ΨFgau(†F_v) restricting to identity (or inverse) on relevant Ψ× copies and compatible with Gv(†Πv)-actions and splittings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These isomorphisms transfer the theta/gaussian formal evaluation structure to the Frobenioid-theoretic side (cf. Corollary 3.6(ii)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Divisibility and infinite-version conventions at Vgood
rubrics_metrics.description: In the Vgood (Vnon) case the monoids Ψenv(Πv), Ψgau(Πv) are already divisible, so one may set ∞Ψenv(Πv) := Ψenv(Πv) and ∞Ψgau(Πv) := Ψgau(Πv); analogous conventions apply for their Frobenioid-theoretic counterparts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This motivates notation for '∞Ψ(−)' used in §3 and simplifies passage to divisible versions in the good-prime case.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prop. 4.3(i) — Aut-holomorphic constant monoids Ψcns(Uv)
rubrics_metrics.description: There is a functorial algorithm in the Aut-holomorphic space Uv for constructing the topological monoid Ψcns(Uv) := A^0_{Uv} (the monoid of nonzero elements of absolute value ≤ 1 of the complex archimedean field), and a tautological isomorphism Ψcns(Uv) ∼→ Ψcns(D_v(Uv)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This realizes the 'constant monoid' in the archimedean/Aut-holomorphic setting (cf. [IUTchI], Example 3.4(i)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Prop. 4.3(ii) — Aut-holomorphic mono-analytic semi-simplifications
rubrics_metrics.description: A functorial algorithm in D_v (or Uv) constructs R_{≥0}(D_v) with distinguished element log_{D_v}(pv); define Ψss_cns(D_v) := Ψcns(D_v)× × R_{≥0}(D_v), and obtain the natural isomorphism ΨR_cns(Uv) ∼→ R_{≥0}(Uv).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is the archimedean analogue of the R_{≥0} semi-simplification and supplies the distinguished log element used in evaluation maps.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prop. 4.3(iii) — Aut-holomorphic labels and F3± symmetrizing isomorphisms
rubrics_metrics.description: For t ∈ LabCusp±(Uv) the action of F3±_v / Gal(Uv/U±_v) induces isomorphisms between labeled monoids Ψcns(Uv)_t for distinct t; these produce diagonal submonoids Ψcns(Uv)(|Fl|) and an isomorphism Ψcns(Uv)0 ∼→ Ψcns(Uv)(F_l).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This mirrors the Πv/Frobenioid label symmetries in the Aut-holomorphic setting (cf. Corollary 3.5).

rubrics_metrics.name: Prop. 4.3(iv) — Aut-holomorphic theta and gaussian monoids and evaluation
rubrics_metrics.description: Define Ψenv(Uv) := Ψcns(Uv)× × R_{≥0}·log_{Uv}(pv)·log_{Uv}(Θ) and Ψgau(Uv) similarly as a product indexed by j∈F_l; one obtains functorial algorithms constructing Ψenv(Uv), Ψgau(Uv) with natural splittings and a formal evaluation isomorphism Ψenv(Uv) ∼→ Ψgau(Uv) mapping formal logs to the tuples (. . . , j^2·log_{Uv}(pv), . . .), restricting to identity on Ψcns(Uv)× and compatible with splittings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is the archimedean analogue of the theta↔gaussian evaluation isomorphism (cf. Corollary 3.5(ii)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Prop. 4.4(i) — Archimedean Frobenioid constant monoid isomorphism
rubrics_metrics.description: The Kummer structure and tautological equalities in the Θ-Hodge theater determine a unique isomorphism Ψ†F_v ∼→ Ψcns(†Uv) of topological monoids (identifying Frobenioid-theoretic monoids with Aut-holomorphic constant monoids).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This uses the Kummer structure †κ_v and the identification †Dv = †Uv to produce the unique identification (cf. IUTchI definitions).

rubrics_metrics.name: Prop. 4.4(ii) — Archimedean Frobenioid semi-simplifications and normalized log
rubrics_metrics.description: There is a unique {±1}-orbit of isomorphisms Ψ×†F_v ∼→ Ψcns(†D_v)× and a unique isomorphism ΨR†F_v ∼→ ΨR_cns(†D_v) mapping the distinguished element (whose natural logarithm equals 1, i.e., pv = e) to the distinguished element of R_{≥0}(†D_v); this yields poly-isomorphisms Ψss†F_v ∼→ Ψss_cns(†D_v) and actual natural isomorphisms after choices.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Normalization (pv = e) is used to fix the distinguished element in the archimedean Frobenioid case.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prop. 4.4(iii) — Archimedean Frobenioid labels and F3± symmetries
rubrics_metrics.description: The isomorphism of (i) determines, for each t ∈ LabCusp±(†Uv), compatible isomorphisms (Ψ†F)_t ∼→ Ψcns(†Uv)_t (well-defined up to an inner automorphism independent of t) and F3±-symmetrizing isomorphisms induced by Gal(†U±_v) actions; these produce diagonal submonoids and an isomorphism (Ψ†F)0 ∼→ (Ψ†F)(F_l).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is the archimedean Frobenioid counterpart of previous label/symmetry assertions (cf. Corollary 3.6(i),(iii)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Prop. 4.4(iv) — Archimedean Frobenioid theta/gaussian monoids and natural isomorphisms
rubrics_metrics.description: Define Ψ†FΘ_v and ΨFgau(†F_v) via the identifications of (i)-(iii); one obtains natural isomorphisms Ψ†FΘ_v ∼→ Ψenv(†Uv) ∼→ Ψgau(†Uv) ∼→ ΨFgau(†F_v) compatible with splittings and restricting appropriately on unit components.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This completes the archimedean Frobenioid transfer of theta/gaussian evaluation structures (cf. Proposition 4.3(iv)).
